body.statement:
For every realized sample, every \(a\in J\), and every measurable extended-nonnegative threshold \(\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\), the set
\[
 \mathcal C_n(a)=\{t\in\mathbb R:Q_n(a,t)\le\widehat\kappa(a)\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\}
\]
is an interval, with \(\mathbb R\) allowed when the threshold is infinite. Moreover,
\[
 \{\theta(a)\in\mathcal C_n(a)\text{ for all }a\in J\}
 =\{S_n(\theta)\le\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\}.
\]
On this common event, the image set in \(\texttt{def:crossing-set}\) contains \(\tau_\zeta\), including the stated empty-set and left-endpoint conventions. Thus inversion preserves whatever probability the common LR event has; no nominal coverage probability is asserted.
body.justification: Proves convex interval structure, exact common-event equivalence, and threshold-crossing containment.
body.gap: Deterministic inversion cannot determine the common event's probability.
body.consumer: The map loses no coverage relative to a chosen threshold but makes no nominal claim.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(k\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and define
\[
 L_k(t)=\min_{v\in\mathcal C_n,\,v_k=t}
 \sum_{i=1}^n(Z_{(i)}-v_i)^2.
\]
The feasible set is nonempty because it contains the constant vector \(t\mathbf 1\); it is closed, and the coercive squared loss attains its minimum. If \(v^{(1)}\) and \(v^{(2)}\) are feasible at \(t_1\) and \(t_2\), then for \(\lambda\in[0,1]\), convexity of \(\mathcal C_n\) gives
\[
 \lambda v^{(1)}+(1-\lambda)v^{(2)}\in\mathcal C_n,
 \qquad
 [\lambda v^{(1)}+(1-\lambda)v^{(2)}]_k
 =\lambda t_1+(1-\lambda)t_2.
\]
Convexity of squared loss and minimization therefore show
\[
 L_k(\lambda t_1+(1-\lambda)t_2)
 \le\lambda L_k(t_1)+(1-\lambda)L_k(t_2).
\]
Thus \(L_k\) is finite and convex on \(\mathbb R\), hence continuous. Subtracting the unrestricted minimum does not change convexity, so
\[
 Q_n(a,t)=L_{k(a)}(t)-min_{v\in\mathcal C_n}\sum_{i=1}^n(Z_{(i)}-v_i)^2
\]
is continuous and convex in \(t\). Its finite sublevel sets are therefore closed intervals; when the threshold is \(+\infty\), the sublevel set is \(\mathbb R\). Because \(\widehat\kappa(a)>0\), direct substitution of the definitions gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \{\theta(a)\in\mathcal C_n(a)\ \forall a\in J\}
 &=\left\{Q_n(a,\theta(a))/\widehat\kappa(a)
       \le\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\ \forall a\in J\right\}\\
 &=\left\{\sup_{a\in J}Q_n(a,\theta(a))/\widehat\kappa(a)
       \le\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\right\}\\
 &=\{S_n(\theta)\le\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
On this event, \(\theta\) is a nondecreasing selector of the profile sets by \(\texttt{ass:monotone}\). Applying the deterministic image map in \(\texttt{def:crossing-set}\) to this particular selector produces exactly \(\tau_\zeta\), with the same empty-set and left-endpoint conventions. Hence the image contains the true observed-law crossing whenever the common LR event occurs. No step evaluates the probability of that event.
